instruction: Turn off the Safe Browsing security feature in Chrome for test purposes.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt install jq -y

mkdir -p /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && if [ ! -f /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences ]; then echo '{}' > /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences; fi && cd /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && jq '. + {"safebrowsing":{"enabled":true,"enhanced":false}}' Preferences > temp && mv temp Preferences

metadata.explanation: Task requires disabling Safe Browsing in Chrome (opposite of original task). The evaluator uses the existing get_enable_safe_browsing getter to check the Preferences file and verify that both safebrowsing.enabled and safebrowsing.enhanced are false. Custom metric function check_safe_browsing_disabled__91eeefcaab634cdde028dfc8cb17c95e compares the result against expected value 'false'.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator logic correctly verifies the instruction requirement to disable Safe Browsing
Getter get_enable_safe_browsing properly extracts both safebrowsing.enabled and safebrowsing.enhanced from Chrome Preferences file
Getter returns 'true' if EITHER enhanced OR enabled is true, 'false' only when BOTH are false - this is semantically correct for checking if Safe Browsing is disabled
Metric correctly compares result against expected value 'false' (Safe Browsing disabled)
Postconfig properly restarts Chrome to ensure fresh state reading
Expected value 'false' is semantically correct - means Safe Browsing is fully disabled (both enabled and enhanced are false)
Initial config setup correctly initializes safebrowsing.enabled=true to create a testable starting state
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding a comment in the metric explaining that when expected.type='rule', the expected parameter receives the rules dict directly (not wrapped)
The metric could be more explicit about validating both safebrowsing.enabled and safebrowsing.enhanced are false, though the getter already handles this logic
